# SOS — Full Card Reference (Visual Grid)

*Every draftable SOS card (341 total) as a tile: image, 17Lands ratings, Draftsim grade /5, expert-guide notes, and an AI take. Ratings: 17Lands PremierDraft (1200-day sample). Generated by `build_card_reference.py`.*

**Legend** — **GIH** = Games-in-Hand WR (primary) · **IWD** = Improvement When Drawn (pp) · **ALSA** = Avg Last Seen At (lower = earlier) · **OH/GD** = Opening-Hand / Drawn WR · **Play** = play rate · **DS** = Draftsim grade /5.  🤖 AI · 📘 Lords of Limited · 🎙 NumotTheNummy · 🎧 Limited Resources.

> **Ordering:** cards within each colour are ranked by a combined **ALSA + play-rate** score (rank-average of the two), not by GIH WR. Both are populated by every draft — where the field takes a card, and how often it makes the deck — so together they track pick priority. A win rate answers a different question: which decks drafted the card.

> SOS is a soup/Converge format — multicolor & Converge win-rates are inflated by 4-5c pilots. The AI take and guide notes decode which deck a number came from.

SOS is a **"soup versus white-X aggro"** format. Strixhaven has five college pairs rather than ten, plus an unwritten sixth archetype — **Converge / 5c soup** — that 17Lands structurally cannot measure, because its record is split across dozens of invisible three- and four-color builds. **The two white colleges are a tier of their own**, 2.3pp clear of third. Note Prismari: last of five *and* the second most-drafted, a quarter of the field in the worst college.

**Archetype win rate** (17Lands PremierDraft, 907,949 two-colour games; share = portion of the two-colour metagame):

| WR | Share | Pair | Plan | Key cards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **57.28%** | 22.1% | **WB** | Silverquill — Repartee aggro/tempo; target your own creatures to grow the board | Scolding Administrator · Render Speechless · Cost of Brilliance |
| 56.89% | 25.6% | **WR** | Lorehold — "leaves the graveyard" value; assertive midrange rather than pure aggro | Rubble Rouser · Molten Note · Pursue the Past · Ark of Hunger |
| 54.57% | 12.1% | **UG** | Quandrix — ramp/fractals. Basically didn't exist as a 2-color deck; feeds soup | Cuboid Colony · Snarl Song · Environmental Scientist |
| 54.05% | 16.1% | **BG** | Witherbloom — lifegain grind or +2/+2-menace overrun | Root Manipulation · Grapple with Death · Bogwater Luminary |
| 54.00% | 23.8% | **UR** | Prismari — spell-density control; the natural soup base, and a trap as a 2-color deck | Elite Interceptor · Tome Blast · Stress Dream · Sanar |

**Removal benchmarks:** Unsubtle Mockery / Tome Blast (R), Last Gasp / Cost of Brilliance (B), Ajani's Response / Repel Calamity (W), Essence Scatter / Brush Off (U), Grapple with Death (BG). **Soup payoffs, and note how late two of them go:** Together as One (the best card in the set), Mathemagics, Snarl Song, **Arcane Omens (wheels to ALSA 5.5)**, **Potioner's Trove (the keystone, wheels to 4.6)**, Sundering Archaic, Divergent Equation, Wisdom of Ages. **Never force soup** — commit only once you have an over-the-top payoff; "bad soup" loses to everything. 17 lands standard, ~7-8 sources per main color.

## Format brief — everything that isn't a single card

The 17Lands numbers on these tiles are the spine of this document — with one large caveat specific to
this set, below. What the three expert guides in `draft-guides/` add is everything a win-rate column
structurally cannot measure: when to commit to a lane, how to sequence around counterspells, how many
sources a splash needs, and how the soup deck actually wins. That is what this brief collects.

**Sources:** Limited Resources (six episodes ending in the #857 Sunset Show), NumotTheNummy (33 VODs
across the full format — the deepest single-set coverage in the repo), Lords of Limited (ten episodes
ending in a 50-takes retrospective). No Limited Level-Ups guide exists for this set.

**⚠ Read the win-rate column carefully here.** SOS is a soup format: a top archetype is a greedy
multicolour pile, and 17Lands splits that deck's record across dozens of invisible three-and-four
colour builds while showing clean two-colour decks in full. The one measurable trace: **colorless
cards post the highest game-weighted GIH WR of any group in the set at 56.6%** — above every actual
colour — because the soup staples (Potioner's Trove, Sundering Archaic, Strixhaven Skycoach, Fields
of Strife, Together as One) are colorless. That is a proxy, not proof, but it points where all three
hosts point.

**Calibrate to the baseline:** the sample is **29.2M games across 327 measured cards**, and
mono-colour game-weighted GIH WR spans only **55.75% to 56.49%** — the tightest colour spread in the
reference. Individual colour differences are near noise. **IWD separates far more cleanly.**

### What the data says

*(The full archetype table with metagame share renders directly above this brief.)*

**The two white colleges are a tier of their own** — the gap from 2nd to 3rd is **2.3pp**, enormous
for a five-archetype format. Limited Resources' settled advice, that if you only care about winning
and the table is open you should be in white-black or white-red, is the plain right answer.

**Prismari is the trap.** Last of the five *and* the second most-drafted at 23.8% — a quarter of the
field in the worst college. If you want a two-colour deck, this is the one to leave.

**Colour order:** **W 56.49 > R 56.04 > U 55.98 > B 55.77 > G 55.75** — a 0.74pp spread, so no colour
is unplayable and none is a lock.

**The soup payoffs, and note how late two of them go:** Together as One (65.6%, IWD **+16.0** — the
best card in the set) · Mathemagics (61.9%, +12.7) · **Snarl Song (61.7%, +11.2 — the best
uncommon)** · **Arcane Omens (59.8%, +9.0, and it still wheels to ALSA 5.5)** · Exhibition Tidecaller
(60.3%, +9.6) · Sundering Archaic (58.8%, +6.9) · Divergent Equation (58.0%, +6.9) · Wisdom of Ages
(57.7%, +7.1).

**Potioner's Trove is the keystone and the field still passes it** — **57.4%, IWD +6.1, 324k games,
ALSA 4.6.** A top-seven common available at pick five.

**Best commons:** Elite Interceptor (59.2%) and Pursue the Past (59.1%, and it wheels to ALSA 5.8)
are effectively tied for first, then Rubble Rouser (57.8%), Unsubtle Mockery (57.5%, IWD +3.9), Last
Gasp (57.4%), Cost of Brilliance (57.4%), Render Speechless (57.4%), Potioner's Trove (57.4%).

### The draft plan

1. **Default to a white college — Silverquill or Lorehold — and let pack one pick the other half.**
   Open a strong white card and see whether black or red is flowing. The gap between the two white
   pairs is 0.4pp, so just take the open one.
2. **Never force soup. It needs a payoff first.** All three sources say this independently, and it is
   the most-agreed claim across them. Commit only once you have at least one over-the-top payoff.
   "Bad soup" — fixing with no payoff, or payoffs with no early interaction — loses to everything.
3. **Take Potioner's Trove and Arcane Omens above where the field takes them.** Both are top-tier and
   both wheel.
4. **Be on the play, and expect long games.** Games run long enough that decking is a real win
   condition and life gain is everywhere, but spending mana every turn still beats the extra card —
   especially with a five-mana hand-emptier legal in every deck.
5. **Prefer the card that does two things.** The reason a soup deck out-cards a grindy deck is that
   its spells are removal *and* draw at once: **Stress Dream (60.1%, IWD +8.6)**, **Traumatic Critique
   (60.3%, +9.8)**, **Stock Up (60.0%, +8.8)**.

### What the numbers can't tell you

- **Don't play around specific answers; do sequence around counter mana.** There are too many possible
  instants per colour to play around any one — make the straightforward play, but split your turn so
  a counterspell only stops half of it.
- **Sandbag your prepared-spell finishers.** The soup decks have to tap low to deploy their payoffs;
  that is the window.
- **Time the mill finisher for a tapped-out opponent, and count their mana first.** Decking is a real
  plan here, not a novelty.
- **Don't run fragile creatures in a spell deck.** Removal is cheap, plentiful and good in every
  colour and rarity — a two-toughness body that isn't doing anything dies for free.
- **Avoid two-toughness creatures that can't grow, especially at three-plus mana.** They fold to the
  cheap red removal and let the slow decks do their thing.
- **Don't fall out of your role.** Aggro must be ahead; soup needs parity; being behind in either is
  where games are lost fast.
- **Quandrix is interaction-starved, not power-starved.** Numot's refinement is the useful one: don't
  force GU tempo — base it blue-red and splash green, or accept you have no removal beyond counters.

### Deckbuilding doctrine

- **17 lands standard. 18 in a shaky soup base or with rummage/pitch outlets. 16 only for tight
  low-curve aggro.**
- **Splash benchmark: roughly 7–8 sources per main colour**, and a single-basic splash is justified by
  about five Converge cards. Two colours wants 2–3 on-colour tapped duals; multicolour wants 4–6.
- **The fixing-when-poor heuristic runs backwards from instinct:** if your mana is already fine, take
  power; the off-colour fixer pays off most exactly when your mana is bad.
- **Great Hall of the Biblioplex beats Terramorphic Expanse for Converge** — 58.8% with IWD +5.9
  versus 56.3% and +2.6. Terramorphic yields one colour and eats a basic; the true five-colour land
  keeps every colour live.
- **Silverquill needs its own targets:** six-plus two-drop creatures and twelve-plus creatures total,
  or your targeted spells have nothing to point at.
- **Card filtering beats raw card advantage**, because hitting land drops matters enormously and there
  is always somewhere to sink mana.

### Where the field misprices cards

- **Cards that wheel and shouldn't** (ALSA 5.5+): **Arcane Omens (59.8% at 5.5, IWD +9.0 — by far the
  biggest gap in the set)**, Pursue the Past (59.1% at 5.8), Cost of Brilliance (57.4% at 6.0), Run
  Behind (57.1% at 5.9, +4.9), Archaic's Agony (56.1% at 6.2, +5.4), Embrace the Paradox (56.3% at
  6.2, +5.2), Quick Study (56.1% at 6.2, +5.1), Masterful Flourish (56.1% at 7.2), Essence Scatter
  (57.0% at 5.1, +5.4).
- **Cards taken early that shouldn't be** (negative IWD by pick 5): Comforting Counsel (45.2%, −6.5),
  Armageddon (51.5%, −3.0), Leech Collector (51.8%, −2.4), Nita, Forum Conciliator (51.4%, −2.3),
  **Forum Necroscribe (51.3%, −1.9)**, Abigale, Poet Laureate (54.6%, −1.6), Joined Researchers
  (54.9%, −1.5), Summoned Dromedary (54.2%, −1.2), **Eternal Student (54.2%, −1.1)**.
- **The whole UR aggro creature suite is below baseline**, which is why Prismari finishes last:
  Deluge Virtuoso 51.9% · Spectacular Skywhale 52.2% · Muse Seeker 52.6% · **Tackle Artist 52.7%** ·
  Elemental Mascot 54.6% · **Expressive Firedancer 55.3%**. The last two are the ones Numot said to
  take every copy of.
- **Daydream (48.8%, IWD −3.9)** is the worst card in the set relative to its reputation.
- **Diary of Dreams (51.7%, IWD +0.4)** and **Root Manipulation (52.7% at ALSA 6.1)** are both
  below-average uncommons despite being pitched as engines.
- **Render Speechless is available, not impactful** — 57.4% GIH but **IWD +0.5 at ALSA 6.6.** You can
  always have one; having it changes little. **Imperious Inkmage (57.2%, IWD −0.2 at 6.6)** and
  **Killian's Confidence (56.5%, −0.1)** share the shape: Silverquill's commons make the deck without
  winning the game you drew them in.
- **Rubble Rouser is the Lorehold engine (57.8%, IWD +2.4 at ALSA 5.1); Garrison Excavator is the
  part you can miss** (56.7%, IWD +0.4).
- **Grave Researcher (55.5% while being taken at pick 2.1)** is a rare you're first-picking for a
  below-average result.
- **The bonus sheet is bimodal — check the tile.** One card per pack, ranging from **Emeritus of
  Ideation (64.5%, IWD +14.5)** down to **Archmage Emeritus (50.0%, −1.5)**. Several bonus-sheet cards
  have samples in the low thousands rather than hundreds of thousands, so their numbers carry far
  wider error bars.

### Open questions the data can't settle

- **How good is soup, really?** All three sources call it the best thing to be doing and all three
  argue 17Lands structurally cannot see it. They are describing a real limitation, not excusing a bad
  take — but note the colour spread is only 0.74pp, so even a large correction doesn't move much.
  The practical synthesis: soup is a real ceiling that needs payoffs first; the white colleges are the
  reliable floor.
- **"Don't pick commons picks 1–8."** One Lords of Limited host holds this hard; the other explicitly
  won't co-sign it. The data can't settle a draft-strategy claim, but note the format's best commons
  (Elite Interceptor 59.2%, Pursue the Past 59.1%, Potioner's Trove 57.4%) beat a great many
  uncommons — so the hard version of the rule costs real equity.
- **Lorehold versus Silverquill.** 0.4pp apart, and Lorehold has the larger metagame share. Genuinely
  too close to call; take the open one.
